role: Commonwealth of Virginia water quality regulatory agency
stance_basis: approves project on condition that separate sanitary and storm sewers are provided
summary: The State Water Control Board, through its Richmond Area representative Mr. L.S. McBride, expressed conditional approval of the Randolph Urban Renewal Project, stating it would not create additional water pollution problems provided that separate sanitary and storm sewers are installed. The document notes the Board has formally approved the Randolph Plan and is cooperating to make the project successful. Their approval is referenced twice in the document window, once as a general statement and once with specific attribution to the representative's letter.
complaint_summary: The State Water Control Board's Richmond Area representative, Mr. L.S. McBride, in a letter dated July 10, 1972, conditionally approved the project, stating it would not create additional water pollution problems if separate sanitary and storm sewers are provided.
summary_quote: The staff is of the opinion that the redevelopment project .proposed will not create any additional water pollution problems if separate sanitary and storm sewers are provided to the fullest extent feasible.

mentions.quote: The Randolph Plan has received the approval of the State Water Control Board.
other official agencies such as the State Water Control Board and Richmond Metropolitan Authority are cooperating to make the project successful.
